question:
A 56-year-old male with a history of bilateral total-knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis 10 years ago is
hospitalized due to a 2-day history of fever and painful swelling in his right thigh. On admission, his
temperature is 38.3°C. Examination reveals a fluctuant nodular lesion with surrounding cellulitis on the
right thigh, but there is no knee pain or erythema. The lesion is incised and drained, and cultures from
the wound and one of two blood culture sets grow methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus*
(MRSA). The patient improves clinically after treatment with vancomycin, with resolution of fever and
improvement of the thigh lesion. A transesophageal echocardiogram shows no vegetations, and repeat
blood cultures drawn 2 days later are negative. Which of the following antibiotic regimens is the most

appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Oral clindamycin for 4 weeks (B) Oral doxycycline for
2 weeks (C) Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for 2 weeks (D) Intravenous dalbavancin for 2 doses
(E) Oral rifampin plus doxycycline for 3 weeks (F) Intravenous ceftaroline for 6 weeks (G) Intravenous
vancomycin for 4 weeks (H) Intravenous vancomycin for 2 weeks followed by oral linezolid for 2 weeks
(I) Intravenous daptomycin for 2 weeks (J) Oral linezolid for 4 weeks
 A. Intravenous vancomycin for 2 weeks followed by oral linezolid for 2 weeks
B. Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for 2 weeks
C. Intravenous daptomycin for 2 weeks
D. Oral doxycycline for 2 weeks
E. Intravenous vancomycin for 4 weeks
F. Intravenous dalbavancin for 2 doses
G. Oral linezolid for 4 weeks
H. Intravenous ceftaroline for 6 weeks
I. Oral clindamycin for 4 weeks
J. Oral rifampin plus doxycycline for 3 weeks
